messages:
Sam (Product): :wave: Quick sync — we need to align on the cross-team deps for the Q3 roadmap slice we're calling 'stretch throughput'. I sketched a priority list in the doc and want owners/ETA: 1) runtime async batching + KV cache changes, 2) infra GPU reservation + burst plan, 3) security KMS/HSM integration for private customers, 4) design QA for fallbacks. Can owners confirm blockers and realistic date windows?
Noah (Eng): I'll take the engineering coord. My take: runtime changes are the biggest unknown (perf regressions risk). Need a canary window and an automated perf check. ETA depends on infra reservations being in place.
Mia (Runtime): For async batching + KV cache tweaks I need a 3-week dev cycle + 2-week canary. Blockers: kernel selection tests and a small model-variant rollout. If infra can guarantee reserved capacity for canary -> earlier.
Leo (Infra): We can provision a reserved pool but need a firm commit: how many GPUs and what sustain QPS? If we overprovision it's costly. What's the minimum for a meaningful canary?
Sam (Product): Good Qs. Minimal canary: 8x A100-equivalent capacity sustained for 2 hours at expected QPS (we estimate ~600 rps peak for the canary scenarios). That would expose batching perf and KV behavior.
Noah (Eng): 600 rps sounds right. Also want autoscaling off for the canary (fixed capacity) to isolate behavior. Mia, can you run the kernel-selection sweeps in parallel with dev work or does it add time?
Mia (Runtime): I can start kernel sweeps in parallel. They'll add ~3 days of CI cycles but won't block initial dev. The real time sink is validating output stability under batching.
Raj (Security): KMS/HSM integration for private customers needs an architecture review and compliance checklist. If customers require customer-managed keys, we need HSM certs + audit plan. Realistically that's 5 weeks from design-to-prod for an MVP (no HSM certs, soft KMS). Full HSM + attestation could be +4 weeks.
Ava (Design): For UX fallbacks, we need a clear error surface and a degraded-mode prompt template. I can produce the QA checklist in 4 working days. We should also test user-visible latency spikes.
Sam (Product): OK — we're hearing: runtime dev 3w + 2w canary, infra reserve scheduling, security 5w for soft-KMS or 9w for full HSM. Prioritization question: shall we launch with soft-KMS (shorter path) and roadmap full-HSM as follow-up? Thoughts?
Leo (Infra): From infra side soft-KMS reduces lift; provisioning reserved pool still needed. If product accepts soft-KMS for initial GA, we can schedule capacity within 2 weeks (pending budget). Full HSM requires procurement lead time.
Raj (Security): Soft-KMS acceptable only if product documents customers that require HSM will be on the later milestone and we gate on contractual terms. We'll need an internal exception path for early enterprise customers.
Noah (Eng): I'm fine with soft-KMS initially as long as we add hooks (abstractions) so switching to HSM doesn't require runtime rework. That adds small engineering tasks but keeps schedule tight.
Mia (Runtime): Agreed. We'll implement a key-provider interface. It adds ~4 dev days. Still within the 3-week dev plan.
Sam (Product): Great. So tentative plan: - Leo: reserve 8 GPUs for canary window in 2 weeks (owner: Leo) - Mia: runtime dev + kernel sweeps (owner: Mia) ETA: 3 weeks dev, 2 weeks canary - Raj: do architecture review for soft-KMS + exception flow, ETA: 5 weeks for soft-KMS - Ava: QA checklist + UX fallback templates in 4 days - Noah: end-to-end canary runbook + perf checks (owner: Noah) Can everyone ack or propose changes?
Leo (Infra): Ack. I'll post cost estimate and reservation PR by EOD tomorrow.
Mia (Runtime): Ack. I have a short checklist I'll drop in the doc, will start tomorrow.
Raj (Security): Ack with note: I'll need product to sign off on customer communication for soft-KMS before canary.
Ava (Design): Ack. I'll add the failover copy + test cases to the doc.
Noah (Eng): Ack. I'll draft the canary runbook and add the perf assertions (95th < 250ms target) and a regression alert.
deploy-bot: Scheduled capacity reservation request created: PR #4123 — awaiting infra approval.
Sam (Product): Thanks all. I'll update the roadmap item with the agreed sequence and owners. Next sync in 5 business days unless blockers pop up. :thumbsup:
